name: Hakvoort Catheter Duration Trial
question: After anterior colporrhaphy, how does catheter removal the next morning compare with removal on postoperative day 5?

arms.label: Catheter removal the morning after surgery

design.population: Women at a Dutch teaching hospital scheduled for anterior colporrhaphy alone or with posterior colporrhaphy and/or vaginal hysterectomy.
design.description: Single-center randomized trial with an equivalence sample-size premise
design.locator: Repository PDF chapter 2, journal pp 828–829, Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Earlier removal increased recatheterization but reduced positive cultures, catheter days, and hospital stay.
takeaway: After anterior colporrhaphy, next-morning catheter removal versus postoperative day 5 increased recatheterization (19/48 versus 4/46) but reduced positive urine cultures (2/48 versus 18/46), mean catheter duration, and hospital stay.

reports.label: Randomized report
reports.citation: Hakvoort RA, Elberink R, Vollebregt A, et al. How long should urinary bladder catheterisation be continued after vaginal prolapse surgery? A randomised controlled trial comparing short term versus long term catheterisation after vaginal prolapse surgery. *BJOG.* 2004;111(8):828-830. doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.2004.00181.x
reports.followUp: Postoperative catheter removal, repeat voiding check after 3 additional catheter days, and index hospital stay
reports.followUpLocator: Repository PDF chapter 2, journal pp 828–830, Methods and Results

results.endpoint: Recatheterization for postvoid residual at least 200 mL
results.measure: Patients requiring repeat transurethral catheterization after first removal
results.note: Odds ratio is prolonged versus next-morning removal, as reported. Sample-size planning allowed recatheterization as high as 50% in the early-removal arm; no formal equivalence result was reported.
results.locator: Repository PDF chapter 2, journal p 829, Table 2 and Results

results.measure: Culture above 10^5 CFU/mL before first catheter removal
results.note: Odds ratio is prolonged versus next-morning removal, as reported. Table 2 prints 18/46 as 40%; direct calculation is 39.1%. Culture positivity, rather than symptomatic UTI, was the measured outcome.

harms.locator: Repository PDF chapter 2, journal p 829, Table 2
harms.note: The paper calls positive cultures urinary tract infections; symptoms and antibiotic treatment were not reported. Its printed 40% for 18/46 differs from the calculated 39.1%.

harms.label: Persistent high residual after the second catheter
harms.locator: Repository PDF chapter 2, journal pp 829–830, Results
harms.note: Residual volume remained above 200 mL in two early-removal patients after three more catheter days; all analyzed prolonged-catheter patients were below 200 mL.

delivery.label: Postoperative catheter protocol

values.exp: 14 Ch transurethral Foley removed the morning after surgery
values.ctl: 14 Ch transurethral Foley removed on postoperative day 5

delivery.label: Voiding assessment and recatheterization
delivery.value: Bladder ultrasound within 8 hours of first catheter removal; postvoid residual at least 200 mL triggered a new transurethral catheter for 3 days, followed by repeat assessment.
